brief: brief-d054-version-slots.md and the lead's follow-up of 2026-11-22. First: the subtest 'an idle worker of another version does not count as a slot for a viewer: a helper is preempted for the next viewer' of TestOutputVersionAcrossProcesses (from JS-082 and JS-087, unchanged since) sets up a lone version-4 worker running the first viewer's job and a helper of that job on the same worker, which D-052 forbids; on the D-052 build it gives up after 1 minute waiting for that helper. Options then: A (the helper is one a second version-4 worker's job is helped by; assertions unchanged), B (keep the check, a lone worker of a version helps its own viewer's job), C (drop the helper from the subtest). Follow-up: with the setup amended (two version-4 workers of one and two slots) and the assertions unchanged, the subtest passes on the D-052 build (27 s) and also on a build that counts every version's workers (33 s), one run each on one host, because the rescue added in the D-052 fix round (a viewer's job that has waited half the queue timeout, 3 s of 6 s, stops the helpers it needs, with the same reason) stops the helper and the viewer still gets a segment; the in-package check of the same invariant does fail on the counting build and passes on the D-052 build. Options now: A (add one assertion: the helper was stopped when the third viewer asked, not by the rescue), B (assertions unchanged, drop the condition that the subtest fails on a counting build, the in-package check being the guard), C (hold #247 for another design across processes).
tradeoff: D-052 and D-053 said the older checks stand unamended but for one subcase; this subtest's setup needs the same-worker helper D-052 gave up, so no build passes both. With the setup amended, its unchanged assertions no longer tell a build that counts the viewer's version only from one that counts every version, because the half-timeout rescue reaches the same end about 3 s later: the proof across processes is kept only by adding an assertion, or given up.
decision: accept (option A of the first brief for the setup; option A of the follow-up for the added assertion)
serves: DOMAINS.md invariant 59: 'Capacity accounting (free cores, helper preemption, `Unavailable`) counts the viewer's version only.' JS-082: 'A slow job's helper is made by a worker of the job's version or by none'. JS-087: 'only live workers and jobs of the replica's output version count'. PRODUCT.md: 'Play starts in seconds and keeps up.' and 'Nothing breaks the viewers' evening. Upgrades, a lost machine and a database failover happen without interrupting anyone.' JS-168 criterion 6: 'A helper is never claimed by a worker that is at that moment running a viewer's, a seek's or a failover's job of its spec.'
entry: The subtest's setup is amended, its assertions are kept and one is added. Setup: two version-4 workers, so the helper holding the slot the third viewer needs runs, by the product's own rule and with no change to the server for the test, on the version-4 worker that is not running the viewer's job; when the third viewer asks, no version-4 worker has the job's cost free without that helper's slot and w5 is idle with room. Assertions kept: the third viewer gets a segment and the helper is cancelled with 'a new viewer needed its slot'. Assertion added: the helper was stopped at the third viewer's ask and not by the half-timeout rescue, read from the rows' own times (the helper ended before the third viewer's job had waited half the queue timeout), with no wall-clock bound of the test's that a slow machine could miss. Conditions: a recorded run of the subtest failing on a build that counts every version's workers, on the added assertion, and a recorded run passing on the build; the in-package check of the same invariant stays unamended and stays shown failing on that build; every other subtest of the test stands unamended; no test-only knob enters the server. If either run does not come out so (the stop and the job's creation being one instant is reasoned, not run), it comes back as a brief with the run's output and option B is not taken by default. It is the second exception to D-052's 'older checks stand unamended', after D-053: JS-168 criterion 6 names it beside the 16-core subcase, and Changed guarantees cites D-054 for the amended setup and the added assertion; any further old check that contradicts D-052 comes back as its own brief (internal/transcode and internal/api were still running when this was first decided). Rejected: of the first brief, B (reopens the regression D-052 closes; no rule separating a lone worker of a version from a lone worker is designed or measured) and C (drops the proof with real processes that a viewer preempts a helper when the only free room is another version's); of the follow-up, B (gives up the proof across processes that version counting is right rather than rescued, when an assertion that keeps it has not been tried: a counting error would delay each start of play by about 3 s during an upgrade and only a one-process check would notice) and C (holds a merge for a design nobody has, while A needs two short runs). Given up: the proof across processes that the lone worker of a version helps its own viewer's job, which D-052 already gave up; in product terms, during an upgrade the last worker of the old version gets no helper for its viewers' job while workers of the new version sit idle, so a job that worker makes below real time stays slow until the roll ends, unmeasured, by viewers on the old version mid-upgrade, number unknown and none known. Nothing viewers have changes by this amendment itself. Noted, not a loss: since the rescue, a version-counting error across processes costs a viewer about 3 s and not a 503 (one run on the counting build), which is why the old assertions alone no longer catch it; the old one-worker setup would be masked the same way (reasoned, not run). Unverified when decided: that the helper's end and the third viewer's job's creation are the same instant on the build, and at least 3 s apart on the counting build; whether in the first failing run a helper row was queued that no version-4 worker could claim, and whether such a row counts against a viewer's room; whether any other old check contradicts D-052; every figure here is one run on one host. Data that reopens it: as D-052 (a measurement of a same-worker helper reaching 1.0x on idle cores; the dogfood showing a job under 1.2x on a worker with the job's cost free and no other worker to help); a capture or dogfood log of a viewer stalled or refused during an upgrade walked in the documented order while the lone worker of its version had the job's cost free, or of a queued helper row that no worker may claim holding room a viewer needed; the added assertion failing on the build in CI for a reason that is the machine's and not the build's; the dogfood's logs showing helpers stopped by the half-timeout rescue while a worker of another version sat idle, which is a counting error the rescue is hiding.
